### 4. compilation-cache-cancellation-coverage-and-entry-guard

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Diagnosis | `CompilationCache.GetCompilationAsync` (`src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/CompilationCache.cs:70-102`) shares one `Task<Compilation?>` across every caller at a given `(workspaceId, projectId, version)` key. The cache-miss branch unconditionally starts `project.GetCompilationAsync(CancellationToken.None)` at line 89 before ever checking the calling caller's own `ct` — so a caller whose token is ALREADY canceled at call time still pays for a full, uncancelable Roslyn compile pass, only to have the result discarded later by `ObserveWithCallerToken` (lines 134-139). This regressed the pre-cache behavior, where an already-canceled token short-circuited before any Roslyn call ran.
